primitives.name: Trust Weight Update Rule
primitives.verbatim_quote: **No update equation, window length, or correlation method is specified.** The build implements an exponential-moving-average accuracy → weight-multiplier rule (documented in `tipster.py` as SPEC, not research).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'w_t': 'trust weight at time t (dimensionless)', '\\alpha': 'smoothing factor (0 < \\alpha < 1)', 's_t': 'signal at time t (dimensionless)', 'o_t': 'outcome at time t (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Trust weight is updated based on past signal-outcome correlation; assumes stationary correlation dynamics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If correlation becomes negative or near-zero, trust weight converges toward baseline.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSE to dynamically adjust source credibility through moving average of signal-realization alignment.

Signal decay is modeled via exponential decay kernels without empirical basis, implying a reliance on speculative defaults. Trust weights derive from a moving average of signal-realization correlation, yet lack formal specification—this introduces a dual failure mode: overfitting to noise and underfitting due to insufficient data. Mirror chains introduce epistemic fragility through unverified third-party inputs. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each component must be rigorously tagged as either SPEC or INFERENCE to avoid laundering hand-set parameters into research findings. The system's robustness hinges on explicit labeling and bounded assumptions.
